chapter: Jelly Roll, Leonard Reed and Chicago mixed crowds
title: Working with Jelly Roll Morton and dating Chicago bands
summary: Punch recalls a year with Jelly Roll and places it after Tiny Parham and Hughie Swift.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: And when you worked with Jelly Roll, would you work all year round?

Well, I didn't work with him but one year. Jelly got down sick or something, and the next year, I don't know, even Bain had this winter part, you know. And Swayze, he taken sick and died. And that was one of Jelly boozing him in, you know. And the other deal was blown in Chicago, playing different spots all around like that. So that's how I let this happen. Jelly just passed out like that, and he died pretty soon. I believe he died in New York though. Didn't die in Chicago, died in New York. But now to tell the truth about that, that was one other, I didn't say I got much money, is that they were out of a bid, but that was the coolest and the easiest job I ever had. How's that? Well, I tell how it was. When we hit a town, we'd go to work at eight o'clock. And we'd work full numbers, take off about ten minutes. We'd go back and work for four more numbers, take off ten minutes. Then we have an hour and a mission, and we'd go back for another half and half and all we were through. And that was every night. I'd wait with rain, you see. And boy, I thought that was mighty good. No way else I'd wait like that.
But when you worked with Jelly, was that after you went with Tiny Palm or before?
Let me get this straight. This year was before I went with Tiny.
No, it couldn't have been. It was after. Yeah, after. Because Tiny, I met them when I first
went to Chicago. Well, was it before you were with Hewitt Swift or after?

This was after Hewitt Swift. Yeah, after Hewitt. Between Tiny, then Hewitt, then Jelly Roll. That's, I think, where I think we... And who came after Jelly Roll? Well, that's when I got rid of this little Louisiana boy, you know.
I see. Well, that gives me a rough idea. Yeah. You know, I like to get the dates on it, roughly.
